## Zeep Lock 0.1.0 — first version
A free, simple password manager for Mac, made to **keep apart what shouldn't be mixed**: work passwords, personal ones, a client project — each in its own vault.
### What you can do
- **Organize by vault.** Create as many vaults as you need (personal, work, a company) and keep each group of passwords separate. - **Store and find quickly.** Title, username, URL, password, notes and tags; search by title and URL; favorites. - **Generate strong passwords** with the length and character types you choose, and see how strong each password is. - **Security audit** to find weak passwords. - **Import and export.** Import from a CSV or JSON file of another password manager; export an **encrypted** backup with a password you choose.
### Security
- Your data is **encrypted on this Mac** with a key protected by your **master password**. The title, URL, tags and name of each vault are encrypted too, not only the password. - The master password **cannot be recovered**. If you forget it, the only way forward is to erase the data on this Mac and start over. Keep it somewhere safe. - Optional **Touch ID** to unlock. - **Auto-lock** after inactivity, and always when the Mac sleeps, the screen locks or the screen saver starts. - The clipboard is cleared after you copy a password, and copied passwords are kept out of the Universal Clipboard.
### iCloud sync (beta)
- It is **optional and off by default**. When on, it keeps your vaults in sync between your Macs using **your own** iCloud account, with the data already encrypted. Zeep Labs has no server of its own and no access to your data. - It is in **beta**: it has not been validated across several Macs yet. Keep an encrypted backup (Settings ▸ Import & Export) and don't rely on sync as the only copy of your passwords.
### Requirements
- macOS 26.5 or later.
### Updates
This version updates itself: when a new one is out, Zeep Lock tells you and you choose whether to install it.
